about: READ-ONLY: renders what `commission-a-disk` WOULD do to a target, and writes nothing. It evaluates exactly the preconditions the write path evaluates — a /dev/disk/by-id/ name for a whole raw disk (not -partN, lsblk type disk, no partitions, no wipefs signature, nothing mounted, not backing /) and an unused /srv/<name> mount path, with /etc/fstab verifying as it stands — and prints a plan document naming the resolved device, every fact it observed, and the act: the parted, mkfs and mount argv and the fstab line the write would add. A target that fails any precondition gets the refusal instead, exit 78, because a plan for something that cannot run is not a plan. No clock in the bytes; its sha256 is printed on stderr as `plan-sha256:`, and that hash is what a passkey signs and what `commission-a-disk` re-renders and compares before it writes (backlog b2d5b546). Declares NO approval: it mutates nothing, and it is the plan_verb the runner renders onto a commission-a-disk request's approve step (q1: the signature binds a rendered plan, not a verb call — a verb call authorises an intent whose target can still resolve differently at execution time, which is exactly how the 2026-09-21 device renumbering would have gone wrong).
